instructor: Patrick is a good teacher, but I think a few points can cause problems for us students. We can never see neither any of our grades nor our attendance rate until the end of the term!!!. Therefore, we cannot use our withdrawal right as we can never see our grades until the summer season starts. He also does not like to teach; he looks as if he wants to leave the class as soon as possible. When I was in the second year, I had taken classes from him, and on some days, he did not come to class because he was always sick, and this year, he did not come to the class on some days because he was ill or he had other excuses. I am curious about what his illness is. He read our essays too late, producing various excuses again. Just because we uploaded it two days late, he read it too late! I do not think he is a successful lecturer. On the contrary, I think he's a really good actor. The course topics were complicated and pretty tough, so it was a terrible situation to try to write on these weird and tough topics that we could never understand. I neither recommend the lecturer nor the course. Patrick returns too late or not at all to the e-mails we send !!! When you ask for feedback, he will either not reply at all or tell you that he will send you an e-mail in the coming days, but guess what happens, he never sends an e-mail and in the end, he does not give any feedback to your essay! I really think Bilkent should be more meticulous in choosing lecturers and consider students' evaluations of lecturers! Otherwise, the students will continue to suffer.

While we were supposed to take 3 hours a week, we only took one and a half hours of class. And in such a case, we were expected to write perfect essays. And we didn't get the grades we deserved; we got very low grades. This is not the UK, and we are having a hard time finding a job in Turkey; taking this into consideration, I recommend that you make a change in the way you teach and your grading style. I don't find the group idea helpful at all because some people don't turn their cameras on at all and in this situation trying to communicate with people is difficult. It was neither helpful nor logical that we had an hour and a half of lessons a week, and for half of that, we were expected to split the class into groups and talk about the topics we never understood throughout the semester. The deadlines on the papers you prepared for the exam are very complicated. There are many deadlines and it's really hard to figure out what to do when. Instead of preparing such long and confusing information papers, if you prepare more understandable and single-deadline papers, it would be much healthier and more logical for everyone! Thank you.
